Read all four verification steps and finite-etale descent/morphism-descent supplier statements. Torsors trivialize over themselves, admit finite affine fppf refinements over affine targets, and descend as finite etale schemes. Actions and equivariant morphisms descend uniquely, so BG is a stack. The Isom sheaf descends from G after a joint trivializing cover; the scheme atlas pulls back to P, finite etale and surjective. The trivial torsor has locally constant left-multiplication automorphisms, and arbitrary torsor inertia is the stated product only for abelian G. Identity group and empty test schemes satisfy the claims. Reader replaced an unrelated Popescu arXiv citation with Stacks 036Z; this is source metadata, while the mathematical finite-etale proof is unchanged.

Read all three steps and every local descent prerequisite. Affine U gives separated R and separated etale projections; j has a closed-graph/etale factorization, so it is separated locally quasi-finite. Pullbacks of the quotient map descend by the reviewed effectivity supplier, then etaleness/surjectivity descend using the preceding local calculation. Only after this does the proof descend diagonal pullbacks from the atlas pair, again using separated locally quasi-finite effectivity. It therefore does not apply the already-algebraic quotient-map lemma circularly. Empty U gives the empty algebraic space. Complete Stacks 0265 proof checked. Read all five steps. Free-cell P is cofibrant in AlgA/B, extension is left Quillen, the kernel equivalence transports cofibrancy, and indecomposables is left Quillen because zero multiplication preserves underlying fibration and weak-equivalence classes. All target modules are fibrant and B plus M -> B is split Kan; the strict enriched adjunction chain therefore represents relative derived derivations. The element 1 tensor p minus epsilon(p) gives the Kahler module modulo I-squared. Comparisons of cofibrant replacements lift against trivial fibrations and form contractible mapping fibres. For ordinary A,B every degree of the cell replacement is polynomial and its augmentation is boundary-trivial, so ordinary cotangent comparison applies. Weak coefficient-base changes and global gluing are explicitly separate. HAG II Proposition 1.2.1.2 and Lemma 1.2.1.3 (PDF 33–34) read; the local strict proof supplies this specialization. Model Statement correction changes none of the actual F2 uses.

Read all four steps. Free diagram Fj is adjoint to evaluation and yields the objectwise lifting classes; evaluation creates sequential colimits for the smallness argument. Objectwise acyclic cells follow from closure of LLP against fibrations, then the same retract proof supplies a projective model. Variable module free sections use sum over arrows of Bt tensor over Bj with M; coefficient extension is left Quillen because restriction creates the underlying lifting and homology classes. Cotensors respect transition maps, and cone restriction preserves objectwise fibrations/trivial fibrations, giving the enriched colimit adjunction. Empty J gives the terminal diagram category and zero extended module colimit. No coherent strictification claim is made. The corrected supplier characterization is consumed via its actual generating sets and corner theorem, so no consumer edit is needed.

Read all three steps and the full current batch-15 quotient-sheaf producer definition. For nontrivial finite constant G, left multiplication on the trivial torsor gives a nontrivial automorphism group over Spec k. Equivalence with a scheme stack would preserve fibre automorphism groups, contradicting this. The trivial-action naive quotient is the terminal presheaf on k-schemes, including empty tests, and is already a represented fppf sheaf. No claim that all k-torsors are trivial is used. The quotient-sheaf supplier is explicitly field-level and matches F3. Reader changes are contract boundary/AC enrichment only; no producer defect found.

Read all four steps. Free-span cell attachments preserve initial cofibrancy and leg cofibrations, so the strict pushout is cofibrant. Its mapping space is a pullback of Kan fibrations. In the path pullback comparison, the constant-path inclusion is a mono; its product with a vertex horn permits a simultaneous lift fixed on that subobject. The retraction takes the lifted endpoint, and max(s,t) gives a simplicial homotopy fixed on the strict pullback. This supplies deformation equivalence, not merely an objectwise bijection. Derived colimit adjunction and replacement invariance give independence. Arbitrary noncofibrant coherent undercategories are explicitly outside this claim. The corrected model characterization affects no actual use; reader changes are contract boundary/choice enrichment.

Each affine quotient is algebraic by the reviewed noncircular affine lemma and embeds as a representable open subquotient. Their sheaf coproduct has a disjoint scheme atlas, and surjective open gluing establishes algebraicity before invoking the already-algebraic quotient-map lemma. The empty scheme is covered by the empty family and produces the empty algebraic space. Choice is inherited from quotient and descent suppliers. Reader changed boundary/AC worksheets only.
